subject: [PATCH 2/3] kernfs: don't lose IN_DELETE_SELF when decoding a file handle

reviews.author: Tejun Heo
reviews.summary: Identified the issue and suggested taking kernfs_rwsem for reading to prevent losing IN_DELETE_SELF notifications. Approved the patch with Acked-by.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Sep 02, 2026 at 09:02:52PM -0700, Shakeel Butt wrote:
> __kernfs_remove() clears i_nlink on the inode each superblock holds for
> the node, and finds those inodes with ilookup().  A lookup that has
> pinned the node but has not put its new inode in the inode hash yet is
> invisible to that pass:
> 
>   CPU0                                    CPU1
>   open_by_handle_at()
>     kernfs_find_and_get_node_by_id()
>       pins the node, still active
>                                           rmdir()
>                                             marks the subtree removing
>                                             ilookup() finds no inode
>     kernfs_get_inode()
>       hashes an inode with i_nlink 1
...
> Fixes: eea5d2bb34ba ("kernfs: Send IN_DELETE_SELF and IN_IGNORED")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Signed-off-by: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>

Acked-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>

Thanks.

-- 
tejun

2026-09-03.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a bug in the kernfs file system where IN_DELETE_SELF notifications are lost when decoding a file handle. The issue arises from the fact that __kernfs_remove() clears i_nlink on the inode, making it invisible to subsequent lookups. The patch takes kernfs_rwsem for reading and ensures that active nodes are not removed during the lookup process.
